description: The reverse-split lifecycle Signal8 has tracked from a company's own SEC filings (proxies, 8-K Items 3.03/5.03/5.07, 6-Ks): one episode per split authority, newest first, each with its state (proposed, vote scheduled, approved, ratio set, effective date announced, charter filed, ... or closed), the ratio or authorised range, meeting / vote / effective dates, the state history, and the events behind it oldest first. Every event carries its source (accession and an EDGAR sourceUrl) and its facts; every stated fact carries the verbatim quote it was read from. Not stated means not measured, not "no": a fact with notStated:true (or a null field) means the documents read did not say it, not that it is false, zero or absent. coverage "unresolved" means the ticker could not be matched to an SEC registrant (not measured). coverage "tracked" with an empty episodes list means no episode has been tracked from the filings read since the tracker started; it is not evidence that no reverse split is planned. effectiveDate is the date the issuer stated, strictly parsed: a scheduled date, not a confirmation that the split happened (it can be postponed or abandoned). A conditional date ("the 25th trading day after the Trigger Event") is returned verbatim in effectiveCondition and is not a date; no date is computed from it. verification is copied from the tracker: "provisional" = one source, not cross-checked (the default, not "doubtful"); "verified" = cross-checked. Approval (present only when approvalAvailable is true): each episode carries approvalPath {path, label, quote, sourceUrl}: shareholder_vote, written_consent, fpi_written_resolution, pre_approved_range (the board set the ratio inside a range shareholders approved earlier), board_only (the company's own filing states no shareholder approval was required, quoted), depositary_ratio_change (an ADS ratio change by the depositary, no shareholder vote, the ordinary shares not consolidated) or unknown. The response also carries domicile {code, label, group, source} (EDGAR, else the latest 10-K / 20-F cover; null = not measured, not "Delaware") and splitAuthority {authority, basis, label, boardMayActWithoutVote, conditions, statute, quote, sourceUrl}. Only basis own_prior_board_only_announcement or charter_clause means the board can split without a vote. authority "unknown" or basis "domicile_default_only" is not a finding about the company: it only states what the domicile's law allows by default (e.g. "Domicile may permit board action; charter not checked"), not that this company can split without a vote. vote_required appears only as a labelled domicile default, not as a statement that a vote is needed. path "unknown" is not "no vote"; a missing proxy does not determine a path. An HTTP 503 FEATURE_DISABLED means the lifecycle tracker is switched off and the response says nothing about the company's splits.
name: get_reverse_split_lifecycle
title: Get Reverse Split Lifecycle
